appraisal_events.evidence: "la « persévérance »... de Mme de Villebon à snober Mme G... ne fut pas tout à fait inutile"; the campaign left Mme G... with a prestige "purement imaginaire" attributed to Villebon, so that she "ne souhaitait véritablement qu'un mari pour sa fille: un fils Villebon", remembering "les avanies hebdomadaires qu'elle avait essuyées rue de Grenelle".
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villebon persistently and visibly snubs comtesse G... whenever they meet at their common cousin's house; the narrator frames this campaign ironically as petty and largely fruitless in itself ("sans résultat"), yet notes it left comtesse G... with an exaggerated, explicitly imaginary sense of Villebon's superiority that later shaped her daughter's marriage choice.

status_effects.explanation: Years of Villebon's contemptuous treatment leave comtesse G... deferring to an unfounded sense of Villebon's prestige, causing her to steer her daughter away from ducal marriages toward a lesser 'fils Villebon' match.

The narrator mocks Villebon's obsessive, largely ineffective snobbery (the weekly éclair-eating near comtesse G..., her private confusion at her cousin's tolerance of her), casting her campaign as petty rather than admirable even though it inadvertently succeeded psychologically.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly calls the prestige Villebon gains in Mme G...'s eyes 'purement imaginaire', so it is unclear whether the passage's dominant irony targets Villebon's petty futility or Mme G...'s unfounded deference; both readings are present and not fully resolved by the text.
